subject: Ecosystem dependency declaration & evidence request
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <security@acme-health.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-health.com (Tom Nguyen)
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Ecosystem dependency declaration request

Hi Lauren,

As part of Acme Health's vendor risk intake for the upcoming SOC 2 review, we need a short "ecosystem dependency declaration" that covers any third-party services, subcontractors, or integrations Redwood relies on that could impact Acme data. Specifically we need:

- A simple CSV with vendor name, primary function (e.g., CDN, monitoring, identity, analytics), country of data processing, whether the vendor sees customer data or hashed/aggregated telemetry, and an owner contact.
- Copies or links to your most recent SOC 2 report (or bridge letter), plus any SIG/CAIQ answers you maintain.
- Confirmation of encryption-at-rest and key management model for customer data (KMS/HSM; who controls keys).
- Any subprocessor agreements or a subprocessor opt-in/notification cadence; if you have a list that changes more frequently than quarterly, note your TTL for the published list.
- A short data flow diagram (high-level is fine) showing where Acme data may touch any external vendor.

Requesting delivery by COB Nov 5 so our audit team can include Redwood artifacts with our intake packet. If you already have a packaged "vendor evidence" bundle, a zip is perfect.

I attached a simple vendor-template.xlsx to show the fields we expect. Let me know if the deadline is an issue.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Director, Security Operations
Acme Health

Status: I started compiling the manifest in the shared Drive. A few clarifications for Acme I think we should answer explicitly:
- Do we consider our telemetry pipeline (hosted with a managed vendor) to be "customer-data" for the purpose of their audit? My read: telemetry is aggregated and non-PII; however some customers configure debug logs that could contain identifiers. We should call that out.
- Key management: our hosted offering uses customer-specific KMS keys with customer control for Dedicated customers; for Hosted customers we hold envelope keys in our KMS (AWS KMS with CMKs). Need to describe this clearly and include relevant diagrams.
- TTL for published subprocessor list: we currently publish an "as-of" list monthly and issue email notices for material changes; recommend stating "monthly publication, emergency notices as needed".

Attachments I'm assembling: redwood_sig_answers_draft.pdf (SIG baseline answers), soc2_link.txt (S3 link + access instructions), and a short PaaS dataflow.png. I'll need Neha to confirm vendor contacts for monitoring and crash-reporting vendors (two vendors) and their country of processing.

Marta — attaching the assembled package for Acme's intake. Contents:

- dependency_manifest_20261102.csv (vendor, function, country of processing, data access level, owner contact)
- redwood_sig_answers_20261102.pdf (SIG baseline answers, marked where we have compensating controls)
- evidence_bundle_20261102.zip (includes SOC 2 bridge letter, PaaS dataflow PNG, KMS architecture diagram, subprocessors addendum template)
- link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-sig (live SIG answers and SOC 2 access instructions)

Quick notes:
- Telemetry: we classify most telemetry as non-PII by default; customers can opt-in to richer debug logs that may include identifiers — we call this out in row 7 of the CSV.
- Key management: Dedicated customers can bring their own keys (BYOK) and manage CMKs; hosted customers use AWS KMS with envelope encryption and our HSM-backed key wrapping.
- Subprocessor publication cadence: monthly (first Monday of each month) with email notices for material updates.

If Acme needs an executed subprocessor addendum or narrower data residency guarantees, let us know and we'll route to Legal & Contracts.

Thanks for your patience — happy to jump on a call to walk through any items.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
